mainTopic: The sources that מילה, and for רבי אליעזר its preparations, override שבת
overview: This amud first finishes רבי אליעזר's view. His source that מילה and its preparations override שבת is the פסוק 'וביום השמיני ימול', and other cases cannot learn from מילה because thirteen בריתות make it unique. The גמרא then asks where we learn that מילה itself overrides שבת, which everyone agrees to. עולא and רבי יצחק say it is a הלכה. That answer is rejected, because רבי אלעזר בן עזריה builds a קל וחומר from מילה to פיקוח נפש, and he holds that no קל וחומר can be built from a הלכה. רבי אלעזר then suggests a גזירה שוה from אות, then ברית, then דורות. Each one fails because of תפילין, an adult's מילה, and ציצית. רב נחמן בר יצחק concludes that all three words together are needed. רבי יוחנן learns it from 'ביום' and defends it against ריש לקיש. רב אחא בר יעקב's source, 'שמיני', is rejected, and a ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן. Finally, רבא questions the flow of that ברייתא, and the גמרא begins rereading it with a קל וחומר from צרעת that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Those Temple services are void once their time passes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes rejecting the attempt to learn רבי אליעזר's rule from time-bound Temple services. Those services expire if their time passes, but מילה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: For they have this special feature: if their time passes, they are canceled.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a rejection that started on the previous amud. The services the גמרא tried to learn from are cancelled once their time passes, so they are stricter about timing than מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those services must be done on their exact day or not at all. That explains why they override שבת. מילה can still be done after the eighth day, so it is not pushed by the same pressure, and the comparison fails.

keyTerms.meaning: since / for they have this feature (introduces what makes a case unique)
its time has passed
it is cancelled / void

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of an argument. The 'it' here is the Temple services from the earlier attempted proof, not מילה. מילה is the case that does NOT become void.

phrases.english: for if its time passes, it is void.
phrases.notes: This finishes the question 'what's special about those cases?', and it shows they can't be compared to מילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the refutation (פירכא) of a derivation begun earlier.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning רבי אליעזר's rule about מכשירי מילה from time-bound Temple services.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Those services are cancelled once their time passes. מילה can be done later, so it has less urgency.

steps.title: A verse is the real source for רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: After that rejection, the גמרא gives רבי אליעזר's real source. The פסוק 'on the eighth day he shall be circumcised' teaches that the eighth day counts even when it is שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is רבי אליעזר's reason: the verse says, 'And on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised', meaning even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier proof failed, so the גמרא switches to a direct פסוק as רבי אליעזר's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ביום' (on the day) stresses that the exact eighth day is required. So מילה happens on that day whatever day of the week it is, even שבת. For רבי אליעזר this also covers the preparations needed for the מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (drops the earlier idea and gives a new one)
this is the reason
for the verse says
and even on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question. If the פסוק is written by מילה, why does the Torah also need to write it by other מצוות?

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer:
for the verse says:
"And on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised"
phrases.notes: ויקרא יב:ג

phrases.english: and even on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected derivation with a direct verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר learns from 'וביום השמיני ימול' that מילה is done on the eighth day even on שבת.

steps.title: Why not write it only by מילה and learn the rest from it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Torah needed to write the 'even on שבת' rule separately by the other time-bound מצוות too (the Temple services from the earlier discussion). It could have written it only by מילה and let the others learn from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah write it only by מילה, and let those other cases come and learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the Torah's wording. It asks why the Torah repeats the idea by other מצוות instead of writing it once by מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that the Torah does not write extra words. If the other מצוות could learn from מילה, writing the rule again by them (for example 'במועדו' by the Temple services) seems unnecessary. The question assumes מילה is a fine model for learning other cases.

keyTerms.meaning: let the Torah (the Merciful One) write
and let these come
and learn from it

phrases.english: But let the Torah write it with regard to circumcision,
and let these others come and learn from it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the parallel verses, given the verse just cited by מילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Torah writing the rule separately (e.g., 'במועדו') by the other מצוות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the other cases could be learned from מילה, writing it by them is extra.

steps.title: מילה is too special to teach other cases
steps.stepSummary: Learning from מילה can be refuted. Thirteen covenants were made over מילה, so it is unique and cannot serve as a model for other מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there is a refutation: what is special about מילה? Thirteen covenants were made over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that other cases cannot learn from מילה because מילה has a unique importance they lack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ברית' (covenant) appears thirteen times in the פרשה of מילה. That gives מילה a special status. Something unique cannot teach about ordinary cases, so the Torah had to write the rule by each of the other cases separately.

keyTerms.meaning: there is room to refute
what about... (opens a refutation by naming a unique feature)
were made (cut) over it
thirteen covenants

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר, the source is the פסוק 'וביום השמיני ימול'. The other מצוות need their own verses because מילה, with its thirteen בריתות, is too unique to teach them.

phrases.english: Because there is a refutation:
What is unique about circumcision? That over it were made
thirteen covenants.
phrases.notes: The word ברית appears 13 times in בראשית יז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: פירכא: shows the learning source is unique
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Other מצוות could learn their override of שבת from מילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: מילה is unique because of the thirteen בריתות, so each case needs its own verse.

steps.title: Where do we learn that מילה itself overrides שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue with רבי אליעזר only about the preparations for מילה. Everyone agrees that the act of מילה overrides שבת. The גמרא asks for the source of that.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים disagree with him only about the preparations for מילה, but about מילה itself, everyone agrees it overrides שבת. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the debate about preparations to the point everyone agrees on: מילה itself overrides שבת. It asks for the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק above was brought for רבי אליעזר's wider view. The חכמים also need a source for the basic rule that the מילה itself is done on שבת. The גמרא is asking what that agreed-upon source is.

keyTerms.meaning: they only disagree to this extent
preparations that enable the מילה (e.g., bringing the knife)
the מילה itself
everyone agrees
from where do we know it?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two topics. The famous argument is about the preparations (מכשירין). The act of מילה on שבת is agreed by all.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ
phrases.english: The Rabbis only disagree with him
regarding the preparations for circumcision,
but circumcision itself,
everyone agrees it overrides Shabbat.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ אֶלָּא בְּמַכְשִׁירֵי מִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from רבי אליעזר's view on preparations to the universally agreed rule about מילה itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the act of מילה overrides שבת, according to everyone.

steps.title: עולא and רבי יצחק: it is a הלכה
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the rule is a הלכה (a tradition from משה at סיני). רבי יצחק says the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: it is a הלכה. And רבי יצחק also said: it is a הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that מילה overriding שבת comes from an oral tradition, not from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הלכה' here means הלכה למשה מסיני, a rule passed down from סיני without a verse behind it. Two אמוראים agree on this. It means the rule is not built from logic or a Torah verse.

keyTerms.meaning: a tradition from משה at סיני (הלכה למשה מסיני)
and likewise said

phrases.english: Ulla said: It is a halakha.
phrases.notes: A הלכה למשה מסיני

phrases.english: And so too Rabbi Yitzchak said: It is a halakha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מילה overriding שבת is a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא builds a קל וחומר from מילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא from a ברייתא. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns that פיקוח נפש overrides שבת through a קל וחומר from מילה, which suggests מילה's rule is not just a הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: From where do we know that saving a life overrides שבת? רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: if מילה, which involves just one limb of a person, overrides שבת, then all the more so saving a life overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge עולא's answer. The full point of the challenge is spelled out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה reasons from a small case (one limb) to a big case (the whole person). That treats מילה's override of שבת as a solid base for a קל וחומר. The גמרא is setting up the question of how this fits with the view that the rule is only a הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
saving a life
one of his limbs
reasoning from the lighter case to the stricter case

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a key early source for the rule that פיקוח נפש overrides שבת.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
From where do we know regarding saving a life
that it overrides Shabbat?
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:

phrases.aramaic: מָה מִילָה שֶׁהִיא אַחַת מֵאֵיבָרָיו שֶׁל אָדָם
phrases.english: Just as circumcision, which involves one of a person's limbs,
overrides Shabbat,
all the more so is it true of saving a life
that it overrides Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: מִנַּיִין לְפִיקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁדּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא and רבי יצחק's answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מילה overriding שבת is only a הלכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא uses מילה's override of שבת as the base of a קל וחומר. The challenge, completed next, is how this fits with עולא's view that the rule is only a הלכה.

steps.title: You cannot build a קל וחומר from a הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the challenge against עולא. If מילה on שבת were only a הלכה, no קל וחומר could be built from it. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה himself taught that rule to רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think it is a הלכה, can a קל וחומר be learned from a הלכה? But it was taught: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said to him, 'עקיבא! That a bone the size of a barley grain makes a person טמא is a הלכה. You want to learn רביעית דם from it by a קל וחומר. But we do not learn a קל וחומר from a הלכה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the attack on עולא. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה used מילה for a קל וחומר, yet he holds that you cannot build a קל וחומר from a הלכה. So for him, מילה on שבת cannot be just a הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הלכה למשה מסיני is a rule handed down orally, with no reason given in a פסוק. So we cannot stretch it further with logic like a קל וחומר. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said this outright to רבי עקיבא about the case of a נזיר. Since he still built a קל וחומר from מילה, he must have held that מילה on שבת comes from the Torah itself.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind (if you were to think)
A bone from a dead body the size of a barley grain. It makes a נזיר טמא, and he must shave.
A quarter-לוג of blood from a dead body
We do not build a קל וחומר from a הלכה למשה מסיני
But it was taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: The case of the bone and the blood is only background. It comes from a debate about a נזיר. The גמרא brings it only to show that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds 'no קל וחומר from a הלכה.' It is not changing the topic away from מילה.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that it is a הלכה (from Sinai),
phrases.notes: Aimed at עולא's position.

phrases.english: can a קל וחומר come from a הלכה?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. The expected answer is no.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said to him: Akiva,
phrases.notes: This is the same תנא who used מילה for a קל וחומר in step 7.

phrases.english: a bone the size of a barley grain makes one impure because of a הלכה,
and you want a quarter-לוג of blood to come from a קל וחומר,
and we do not derive a קל וחומר from a הלכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ הֲלָכָה — קַל וָחוֹמֶר מֵהֲלָכָה מִי אָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 7 by supplying the principle that makes it a real contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that מילה overriding שבת is a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה builds a קל וחומר from מילה. He also holds that a קל וחומר cannot be built from a הלכה. So for him, מילה on שבת must come from a פסוק, not a הלכה.

steps.title: A new source: the word 'sign' by both מצוות
steps.stepSummary: עולא's answer is set aside. רבי אלעזר says we learn it from a גזירה שוה: the word אות appears by מילה and by שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אלעזר said: we learn it from 'sign' and 'sign.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the הלכה answer fell, the גמרא gives a new answer to the question from step 5. It is a גזירה שוה from the word אות, which appears by both מילה and שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By מילה the Torah says 'it shall be a sign of the covenant.' By שבת it says 'for it is a sign between Me and you.' Linking the two words teaches that one sign, מילה, may be done on the day of the other sign, שבת. This gives מילה a source in the פסוקים, which fits רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the previous answer and offers a new one.
It comes (is learned) from, usually by a גזירה שוה
Sign. The shared word by מילה and שבת.
Learning a law from the same word used in two places in the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: This is רבי אלעזר (a later אמורא), not רבי אלעזר בן עזריה from the ברייתא. The names are close but they are different people.

phrases.english: Rather, רבי אלעזר said:
It is derived from 'sign' and 'sign.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:11 (מילה) and שמות 31:13 (שבת).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces עולא's rejected answer with a source from the פסוקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the act of מילה overrides שבת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the word אות, found by both מילה and שבת

steps.title: Then תפילין should also override שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the אות source. תפילין are also called an אות, yet nobody says they override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, תפילין are also called 'sign' in the Torah. They should override שבת too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's גזירה שוה. It proves too much, because it would also let תפילין push aside שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אות is not unique to מילה. The Torah also calls תפילין a sign ('it shall be for a sign on your hand'). If sharing the word אות were enough, תפילין would override שבת too, and that is not the הלכה. So the word אות cannot be the real link.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (now that you say this). It introduces a strange result of the previous idea.
Tefillin. Also called an אות in the Torah.
They should push aside (override) שבת

phrases.english: But if so,
תפילין, about which 'sign' is written,
phrases.notes: שמות 13:16.

phrases.english: should override שבת!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, תְּפִילִּין דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ ״אוֹת״, לִידְחֵי שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the גזירה שוה proposed in step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word אות also appears by תפילין. The same reasoning would make תפילין override שבת, which is clearly wrong.

steps.title: The real source: the word 'covenant'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא switches to a גזירה שוה from the word ברית, which appears by מילה and by שבת but not by תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we learn it from 'covenant' and 'covenant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by using a different shared word. ברית appears by both מילה and שבת, so מילה overrides שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By מילה the Torah says 'a sign of the covenant.' By שבת it says 'for a perpetual covenant.' תפילין are never called a ברית, so the תפילין challenge no longer applies. The next step challenges this new source too.

keyTerms.meaning: Covenant. The shared word by מילה (Genesis 17:11) and שבת (Exodus 31:16).

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's 'הלכה' answer was rejected, and the אות-אות answer failed because of תפילין. The ברית-ברית answer is challenged in the very next step, and the final answer comes in step 15.

phrases.english: Rather, it is derived from 'covenant' and 'covenant.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:11 (מילה) and שמות 31:16 (שבת).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תפילין challenge by replacing אות with ברית as the linking word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the derivation with a different shared word that excludes the problem case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The shared word אות links מילה to שבת, but then תפילין would also override שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shared word is ברית, which is not written by תפילין, so תפילין are not included. The next step shows that ברית also applies to an adult's מילה.

steps.title: An adult's circumcision also has the word covenant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברית source. The מילה of an adult is also called a ברית, so his מילה should override שבת too. But it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: An adult, about whom 'covenant' is also written, should override Shabbat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 11, which learned from the word ברית. If ברית is the source, then an adult's מילה should also override שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of ברית applies to every Jewish male who is not yet circumcised, even an adult. Yet the הלכה is that only מילה on the eighth day overrides שבת. So the word ברית proves too much and cannot be the whole source.

keyTerms.meaning: An adult, here meaning a Jewish male who was not circumcised on his eighth day
About whom it is written
Let it override שבת. This is a challenge form meaning 'then it should override שבת!'

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying an adult's מילה is not a real ברית. It is a full מצוה of ברית. It simply does not override שבת, because only מילה at its fixed time (the eighth day) does.

phrases.english: An adult, about whom 'covenant' is written,
phrases.notes: An adult's circumcision is also part of the covenant of מילה.

phrases.english: let it override Shabbat!
phrases.notes: But it does not, so the ברית source is too broad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברית גזירה שוה offered in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה from the word ברית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word ברית also covers an adult's מילה, which does not override שבת. So ברית alone cannot be the reason מילה overrides שבת.

steps.title: Switching to the word generations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops ברית and learns from the word דורות, which appears by מילה and by שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is learned from 'generations' and 'generations'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new source. It learns from the word דורות, which appears both by מילה and by שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word דורות appears by שבת (שמות ל״א:ט״ז) and by מילה (בראשית י״ז). This new link is meant to point to the regular eighth-day מילה and avoid the adult problem from Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is coming.
It comes from, meaning it is learned from
Generations, a word in the פסוקים about מילה and about שבת

phrases.english: Rather, it is derived from 'generations' and 'generations'.
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word appears by שבת and by מילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge in Step 12 by replacing the ברית source with a דורות source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the source with a different shared word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word ברית alone shows that מילה overrides שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source is the word דורות, shared by מילה and שבת.

steps.title: ציצית also has the word generations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the דורות source. ציצית is also described with the word דורות, yet it does not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tzitzit, about which 'generations' is written, should override Shabbat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new דורות source. The פסוק about ציצית also says 'throughout their generations'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word דורות were enough, then tying ציצית onto a garment would be allowed on שבת. Nobody says that. So דורות alone also proves too much.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual fringes on a four-cornered garment, also described with the word דורות in the Torah

phrases.english: Tzitzit, about which 'generations' is written,
phrases.notes: The פסוק says 'and they shall make for themselves tzitzit throughout their generations' (במדבר ט״ו:ל״ח).

phrases.english: let it override Shabbat!
phrases.notes: But ציצית does not override שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the דורות source from Step 13 with the same kind of challenge used against אות and ברית.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה from the word דורות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ציצית shares the word דורות but does not override שבת. So דורות alone cannot be the source.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק combines all three words
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that we learn from all three words together: אות, ברית, and דורות. מילה and שבת share all three. תפילין and ציצית each have only one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We derive 'sign', 'covenant' and 'generations' from 'sign', 'covenant' and 'generations', to exclude these, since only one word is written about each of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the final answer. Every earlier challenge is solved by requiring all three shared words at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The single-word links failed because other מצוות also had the word: אות by תפילין and דורות by ציצית. Requiring all three words together excludes תפילין and ציצית, since each of them has only one. The גמרא names only these two cases ('הנך') as excluded by the three-word rule.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive, we learn one case from another
To exclude
These, meaning the cases raised in the challenges
Only one each. Each of those cases has just one of the three words.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן בר יצחק, מילה overrides שבת because it shares three words with שבת: אות, ברית, and דורות. No single word is enough, because תפילין (אות) and ציצית (דורות) each share only one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear example of the גמרא building a stronger source after each weaker one is knocked down. It also explains why מילה, and not other מצוות with similar words, overrides שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
phrases.notes: The earlier single-word answers are dropped.

phrases.english: We derive 'sign', 'covenant' and 'generations'
phrases.notes: These are the three words written about מילה.

phrases.english: from 'sign', 'covenant' and 'generations',
phrases.notes: The same three words are written about שבת.

phrases.english: to exclude these,
phrases.notes: These are תפילין and ציצית.

phrases.english: since only one word is written about each of them.
phrases.notes: Each excluded case shares just one of the three words with שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: דָּנִין ״אוֹת״ ״בְּרִית״ וְ״דוֹרוֹת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ציצית challenge in Step 14. It also closes the whole chain of challenges from Steps 10 to 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining several shared words so the source is narrow enough
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One shared word (אות, ברית, or דורות) is enough to make the link.
steps.terutzMaskana: All three words together are needed. Only מילה and שבת share all three.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מילה at its proper time overrides שבת through a three-word link (אות, ברית, דורות). Cases with only one of these words are excluded.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן learns from the word on the day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a new source: the פסוק says ביום, and that means the eighth day, even if it is שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The פסוק says: on the day. On the day means even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a brand-new way to prove that מילה overrides שבת. רבי יוחנן points to one word in the פסוק: ביום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא says the baby is circumcised ביום השמיני, on the eighth day. רבי יוחנן reads the extra stress on the day to mean: whatever day the eighth day falls on, even שבת. This is a separate approach from the אות, ברית, דורות method.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל
The פסוק says (introduces a source)
On the day
Even on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not answering the earlier challenges. He is giving his own separate source for the whole הלכה that מילה overrides שבת.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The verse says: on the day.
phrases.notes: ויקרא יב:ג, וביום השמיני ימול

phrases.english: On the day means even on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a separate source instead of the אות, ברית, דורות derivation from Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word ביום teaches that מילה is done on the eighth day even when it falls on שבת.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks about those still lacking atonement
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges: the word ביום is also written by מחוסרי כפרה, so their קרבנות should override שבת too. But they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: If so, מחוסרי כפרה, about whom ביום is also written, should their קרבנות also override שבת?!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן's source. If ביום means even on שבת, it should mean that in other places too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מחוסרי כפרה (like a זב or a healed מצורע) bring their קרבנות on the eighth day, and the פסוק there also says ביום. Yet everyone agrees those קרבנות do not override שבת. So ביום alone cannot mean even on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי שמעון בן לקיש, רבי יוחנן's main study partner
But if so, then (introduces a challenge from a consequence)
People who still need to bring a קרבן to finish their purification
That they override שבת

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan:
But if so, those lacking atonement,
about whom on the day is written,
phrases.notes: ויקרא יד:י, the eighth day of the מצורע

phrases.english: would they also override Shabbat?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ביום source from Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading of ביום as even on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears by מחוסרי כפרה, but their קרבנות do not override שבת, so the word cannot carry that meaning.

steps.title: That verse teaches day and not night
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers: ביום by מחוסרי כפרה is needed for something else, to teach that the קרבן is brought by day and not at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed to teach: by day and not at night.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends himself. By מחוסרי כפרה, the word ביום is already busy teaching a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word used to teach one law is not free to teach another. By מחוסרי כפרה, ביום teaches that the קרבן must be brought in the daytime. So it says nothing about שבת there.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed (for a different teaching)
By day and not at night

phrases.english: That one is needed
for: by day and not at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ בַּיּוֹם וְלֹא בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is used up for a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ביום by מחוסרי כפרה should teach even on שבת, just like by מילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: By מחוסרי כפרה, ביום teaches only day and not night.

steps.title: The circumcision verse should also mean day and not night
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש turns it around: then ביום by מילה should also just teach day and not night, not even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This word too is needed to teach: by day and not at night!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש uses רבי יוחנן's own answer against him. If ביום means daytime by קרבנות, it should mean daytime by מילה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה also must be done by day. So the word ביום by מילה may simply teach that, leaving nothing to teach about שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: This one also

phrases.english: This one too is needed
for: by day and not at night!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי נָמֵי, מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ בַּיּוֹם וְלֹא בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 18 back onto his own source in Step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ביום teaches daytime by קרבנות, it should teach daytime by מילה too, so it is not free to teach even on שבת.

steps.title: Daytime for circumcision comes from eight days old
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers: the daytime rule for מילה comes from a different פסוק, בן שמונת ימים, so ביום is free to teach even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: That law comes from the פסוק: one who is eight days old.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן shows that for מילה, the daytime rule already has its own source. So the word ביום is left free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in בראשית says בן שמונת ימים, eight days old, and ימים (days) teaches daytime. Since daytime is already covered, ביום in ויקרא is extra and teaches even on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Eight days old (בראשית יז:יב)
It comes out (is derived)

steps.confusionAlert: Two different פסוקים about מילה are in play here: ביום השמיני in ויקרא and בן שמונת ימים in בראשית. One teaches daytime, the other is then free to teach even on שבת.

phrases.english: That law comes out of the verse: eight days old.
phrases.notes: בראשית יז:יב

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different פסוק covers the other law, freeing the word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ביום by מילה is used up teaching daytime.
steps.terutzMaskana: Daytime for מילה comes from בן שמונת ימים, so ביום teaches even on שבת.

steps.title: Daytime for offerings also has its own verse
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש pushes back: the daytime rule for קרבנות also has its own source, ביום צותו, so ביום by מחוסרי כפרה should be free to teach even on שבת too.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one too comes from: on the day He commanded!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש uses רבי יוחנן's own method again. If daytime for קרבנות has its own פסוק, then the original challenge from מחוסרי כפרה comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא ז says ביום צותו, on the day He commanded, which teaches that all קרבנות are brought by day. So ביום by מחוסרי כפרה is just as free as by מילה, and should teach that their קרבנות override שבת. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: On the day He commanded (ויקרא ז:לח), source that קרבנות are brought by day

steps.whyThisMatters: This brings the whole discussion back to ריש לקיש's first challenge in Step 17, so רבי יוחנן's source again needs defending.

phrases.english: This too comes out of the verse: on the day He commanded!
phrases.notes: ויקרא ז:לח

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the method of Step 20 against the answer in Step 18, reviving the challenge of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's answer that ביום by מחוסרי כפרה teaches only day and not night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Daytime for all קרבנות is already learned from ביום צותו, so ביום by מחוסרי כפרה is free and should teach even on שבת, which is not the הלכה.

steps.title: The extra 'ביום' by מחוסרי כפרה is still needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers ריש לקיש: even though ביום צותו already teaches 'day, not night' for קרבנות, the ביום by מחוסרי כפרה is still needed. Without it, we might think that because the Torah is merciful to them, they may also bring their קרבן at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though the rule comes from 'on the day He commanded,' an extra source was still needed. You might have thought: since the Torah had mercy on him and let him bring a cheaper offering of poverty, let him also bring it at night. So the verse teaches us that he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. It explains why the word ביום by מחוסרי כפרה is still busy teaching 'by day,' so it cannot be used to teach 'even on שבת.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said ביום by מחוסרי כפרה is a spare word, since ביום צותו already teaches daytime. The answer is that מחוסרי כפרה are a special case. The Torah already went easy on them by allowing a cheaper offering, so we might have assumed it also lets them bring it at night. The extra ביום is needed to block that idea, so it is not spare.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On the day He commanded' — the general source that קרבנות are brought by day
It was needed — the word is not extra
You might have thought — introduces a mistaken assumption (הוה אמינא)
Poverty — the cheaper offering allowed for some מחוסרי כפרה
It teaches us — the verse rules out the mistaken assumption

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new rule that קרבנות are brought by day. Everyone already knows that from ביום צותו. The point is only that מחוסרי כפרה might have been an exception because the Torah shows them mercy, so their ביום is needed.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּנָפְקָא מִ״בְּיוֹם צַוּוֹתוֹ״,
phrases.english: Even though it is derived from "on the day He commanded,"
it was still needed.
phrases.notes: The ביום by מחוסרי כפרה is still necessary.

phrases.english: It might have entered your mind to say:
since the Merciful One had pity on him
to bring an offering of poverty,
phrases.notes: A cheaper offering, such as birds instead of animals.

phrases.english: let him also bring it at night,
so it teaches us that he may not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּנָפְקָא מִ״בְּיוֹם צַוּוֹתוֹ״, אִצְטְרִיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge in step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the word is needed for a special case (mercy-based הוה אמינא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the Torah is merciful to מחוסרי כפרה, maybe they may bring their קרבן at night too.
steps.terutzMaskana: ביום by מחוסרי כפרה is needed to teach 'day only' for them as well, so it cannot teach 'even on שבת.'

steps.title: רבינא: then a זר or an אונן should be allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבינא attacks the mercy logic. If the Torah's mercy could make the rules easier for מחוסרי כפרה, then a זר and an אונן should also be allowed to offer their קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objected: But if that is so, a non-כהן should be fit to bring these offerings, and an אונן should be fit to bring them too!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the reasoning of the last step. He argues that the 'mercy' idea goes too far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step said we might think mercy allows night offerings. רבינא says that if this logic were real, it would allow other leniencies too, such as letting a זר or an אונן offer them. That cannot be right, so the הוה אמינא seems flawed, and then the extra ביום would seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected — introduces a sharp challenge
But if so — 'follow your logic and see where it leads'
A non-כהן, who normally may not do the עבודה
A mourner on the day of a close relative's death, who normally may not do the עבודה

phrases.english: Ravina strongly objected to this:
But if that is so,
a non-priest should be fit to offer them,
and an acute mourner should be fit to offer them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הוה אמינא used in step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The mercy-based הוה אמינא in step 22
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio: if mercy allowed night offerings, it should also allow a זר or an אונן. That is absurd, so the הוה אמינא is weak.

steps.title: The verse brought them back to the normal rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the extra פסוק (ביום) returns these קרבנות to the regular rules. The Torah is only lenient where it says so explicitly, and otherwise they follow all the normal laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse brought it back to the normal rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא in one short line. The extra ביום is exactly what tells us not to stretch the mercy idea any further.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא asked why we would not also allow a זר or an אונן. The answer is that the extra ביום is what 'restored' these קרבנות to normal status. Without it, the mercy idea really could have spread. That is why the word was needed, so the הוה אמינא in step 22 holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse returned it — brought it back to the normal rules

phrases.english: The verse has restored it to the normal rules.
phrases.notes: The extra ביום teaches that the leniency applies only where the Torah states it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge in step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra verse limits the leniency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mercy might relax every rule for these קרבנות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra ביום returns them to all the normal rules, so a זר and an אונן remain unfit, and night offerings are not allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's source stands: ביום by מחוסרי כפרה is needed to keep their קרבן normal (day only), while ביום by מילה is free to teach 'even on שבת.'

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: the word 'eighth' teaches מילה even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a different source for מילה overriding שבת. The verse says 'the eighth' day, which means the eighth day no matter what, even if it is שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: The verse says 'eighth.' The eighth day, even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא offers another way to learn that מילה pushes aside שבת. This time the source is the word שמיני, not the word ביום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is 'וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי יִמּוֹל.' רב אחא בר יעקב reads the emphasis on 'eighth' as meaning the exact eighth day always, so even שבת does not push it off. This approach avoids the whole ביום debate between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says — introduces a פסוק as a source
Eighth — the day of מילה
Even on שבת

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
The verse says: "eighth."
"Eighth" — even on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source from רבי יוחנן's ביום
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה is done on the eighth day even when it falls on שבת, learned from the word שמיני.

steps.title: But 'eighth' is needed to rule out day seven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב. The word שמיני is needed to teach that מילה cannot be done earlier, on the seventh day, so it cannot also teach 'even on שבת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This word 'eighth' is needed to exclude the seventh day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new source. It claims the word שמיני already has a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word can only teach one extra lesson. The challenge says שמיני is needed to teach 'not before day eight,' so it is not free to teach 'even on שבת.' This is the same kind of attack ריש לקיש used against ביום.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for — the word is already being used for another lesson
To exclude
The seventh day

phrases.english: This word "eighth" is needed
to exclude the seventh day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אחא בר יעקב's source in step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's use of שמיני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is already used up teaching 'not on day seven,' so it cannot teach 'even on שבת.'

steps.title: Day seven is ruled out by 'בן שמונת ימים'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule against day seven comes from a different פסוק, 'בן שמונת ימים.' So שמיני is free to teach 'even on שבת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule against the seventh day comes from 'he that is eight days old.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אחא בר יעקב. It shows that the 'not on day seven' rule already has its own source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in בראשית, 'וּבֶן שְׁמֹנַת יָמִים יִמּוֹל,' already teaches that a baby must be eight days old. So the word שמיני in ויקרא is not needed for that, and it is free to teach that מילה happens even on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Eight days old (בראשית יז:יב) — the source that מילה is not done earlier
It is derived from

steps.whatToRemember: For now, רב אחא בר יעקב's שמיני survives, because day seven is ruled out by בן שמונת ימים. The next step challenges this answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: The defense of רב אחא בר יעקב copies the move used for רבי יוחנן in step 20: send the competing lesson to בן שמונת ימים. Step 28 shows why that move fails here.

phrases.english: The seventh day is excluded by "he that is eight days old."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to another source for the competing lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמיני is needed to rule out day seven.
steps.terutzMaskana: Day seven is ruled out by בן שמונת ימים, so שמיני teaches 'even on שבת.'

steps.title: Both verses are needed, one against day seven and one against day nine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 27. 'בן שמונת ימים' and 'שמיני' are both still needed. One rules out circumcising on day seven, and the other rules out pushing it off to day nine. So 'שמיני' is not free to teach 'even on שבת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But you still need both verses. One rules out the seventh day, and one rules out the ninth day. If we had only one verse, I would have said: on the seventh day you cannot circumcise, because his time has not come yet. But from the eighth day and on, it is his time, so day nine would be fine too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. It says the second פסוק is not extra after all, because each verse has its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said 'בן שמונת ימים' rules out day seven, so 'שמיני' is free to teach 'even on שבת.' The גמרא now says one verse alone could only stop us from going too early (day seven). We would still think day nine is allowed, since the time has already arrived. So the second verse is needed to fix the מילה to day eight exactly, and nothing is left over for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: But still / yet — opens a further challenge
To exclude / to rule out
The seventh day
The ninth day
Its time has not yet arrived

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think ruling out day seven automatically rules out day nine. Going too early and going too late are two separate issues. One verse only covers 'too early,' so a second verse is needed for 'too late.'

phrases.english: But it is still needed —
phrases.notes: Both verses are still needed for other purposes.

phrases.english: one to exclude the seventh day,
and one to exclude the ninth day.
For if we had only one verse, I would have said:
it is the seventh day that is excluded, because its time has not arrived,
but from the eighth day and onward, it is its time!
phrases.notes: So without a second verse, day nine would be allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ, חַד לְמַעוֹטֵי שְׁבִיעִי, וְחַד לְמַעוֹטֵי תְּשִׁיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 27, which claimed 'שמיני' was free to teach 'even on שבת.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 27 that 'בן שמונת ימים' alone handles the timing, leaving 'שמיני' free for שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One verse can only rule out going early (day seven). A second verse is needed to rule out going late (day nine). So both verses are used up, and no verse is left to teach 'even on שבת.'

steps.title: Conclusion: the source is like רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found for רב אחא בר יעקב. The גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן's source is the clear one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that the source is like רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on רב אחא בר יעקב's source. It says רבי יוחנן's source is the correct one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא בר יעקב's source ('שמיני') was shown to be needed for timing (Step 28). So we go back to רבי יוחנן, who learns that מילה overrides שבת from the word 'ביום.'

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear — the גמרא's way of settling on one view after the other failed

steps.whatToRemember: The source that מילה overrides שבת is 'ביום' (like רבי יוחנן), not 'שמיני' (like רב אחא בר יעקב), because 'שמיני' and 'בן שמונת ימים' are both needed to fix the exact day.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear that it is like רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after the challenge in Step 28 is left unanswered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אחא בר יעקב's source is rejected. The source for מילה overriding שבת is רבי יוחנן's 'ביום.'

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן and not רב אחא בר יעקב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא first suggests 'שמיני' teaches 'even on שבת.' Then it asks whether the שבת prohibition might block מילה instead. It settles the question only with 'ביום.' This matches רבי יוחנן and goes against רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that fits רבי יוחנן and not רב אחא בר יעקב: 'On the eighth day he shall be circumcised' means even on שבת. So how do I keep 'whoever desecrates it shall surely die'? That is about other forbidden work, not מילה. Or maybe it is not so, and it includes even מילה. Then how do I keep 'on the eighth day he shall be circumcised'? When it is not שבת. The verse says 'on the day' — even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support for רבי יוחנן. The ברייתא does not rely on 'שמיני' alone, and it only settles the question with 'ביום.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that 'שמיני' alone cannot decide the question, because you could read it as 'except on שבת.' Only 'ביום' proves that מילה is done even on שבת. That is exactly רבי יוחנן's source, so this ברייתא backs him and goes against רב אחא בר יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in line with him — a supporting source
And how do I fulfill — how do I give the other verse a meaning?
Whoever desecrates it (שבת) shall surely die
The verse teaches / therefore the Torah says
On the day — the word רבי יוחנן uses as his source

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא settles the debate between רבי יוחנן and רב אחא בר יעקב from a תנאי source, not just from reasoning.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רבי יוחנן,
and not in line with רב אחא בר יעקב:
'On the eighth day he shall be circumcised' — even on שבת,
and how do I fulfill 'whoever desecrates it shall surely die'?
It refers to other forbidden labors, except for מילה.
Or perhaps it is not so, and it includes even מילה,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא flips the reading the other way.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים ״שְׁמִינִי יִמּוֹל״ — חוּץ מִשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: and how do I fulfill 'on the eighth day he shall be circumcised'? When it is not שבת,
therefore the verse says: 'on the day' — even on שבת.
phrases.notes: The decisive source is 'ביום', like רבי יוחנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וּדְלָא כְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings תנאי support for the conclusion in Step 29.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that 'ביום' is the source for מילה overriding שבת, against רב אחא בר יעקב's 'שמיני.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that finds 'שמיני' unclear (it could mean 'except on שבת') and settles the question only with 'ביום.'

steps.title: רבא asks why the ברייתא changed its mind without reasons
steps.stepSummary: רבא questions the flow of the ברייתא. First it seemed happy that 'שמיני' teaches 'even on שבת.' Then it suddenly doubted that reading, but gave no reason either for accepting it or for doubting it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This תנא — at first, what made him comfortable? And at the end, what bothered him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a problem with how the ברייתא is built. He says it shifts from one reading to the opposite with no explanation, and this sets up the גמרא's rereading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first read 'שמיני' as 'even on שבת' and limited the death penalty to other work. Then it reversed with 'or perhaps' and offered nothing new. רבא wants to know what logic stood behind the first reading and what new problem caused the switch.

keyTerms.meaning: At first / originally
It was acceptable to him / it sat well with him
And in the end

phrases.english: רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי קָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: This תנא — at first, what was acceptable to him,
and in the end, what was difficult for him?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי קָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ, וּלְבַסּוֹף מַאי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the internal logic of the ברייתא brought in Step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The flow of the ברייתא in Step 30.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא accepts a reading and then rejects it with no reason given for either move, so its argument seems to have no basis.

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא: מילה overrides שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain what the ברייתא really means. It starts by restating the first reading: 'שמיני' means even on שבת, the death penalty is only for other work, and מילה overrides שבת. The explanation continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it is saying: 'On the eighth day he shall be circumcised' — even on שבת. And how do I fulfill 'whoever desecrates it shall surely die'? With other forbidden labors, except מילה. But מילה overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer רבא by rereading the ברייתא step by step. This step only covers the first part, and the explanation continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא restates the ברייתא's first reading and adds a clear statement: 'אבל מילה דחיא.' This frames the opening line as a full position that מילה pushes aside שבת. The reason behind it, and why the ברייתא later doubts it, will come in the following lines.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means — introduces a rereading of a source
Overrides / pushes aside

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
'On the eighth day he shall be circumcised' — even on שבת.
And how do I fulfill 'whoever desecrates it shall surely die'?
With other forbidden labors, except for מילה,
but מילה overrides שבת,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering רבא's question from Step 31 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא's wording to show its logical flow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to switch readings with no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's first line is a real position: 'שמיני' teaches that מילה overrides שבת. The reasoning for this, and for the later doubt, continues in the next lines.

steps.title: Why did the ברייתא first accept that reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reasoning made the ברייתא comfortable, at first, with saying that מילה overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא's first reading made sense to it. This short question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא complained in Step 31 that the ברייתא gave no reason for its first reading. Now the גמרא starts to supply that missing reason. So this question is the first part of the answer to רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? A request for the logic behind a position.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Asks why the ברייתא at first assumed that 'שמיני' means even on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation begun in Step 32 by asking for the logic behind the ברייתא's first reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning that made the ברייתא at first think that מילה overrides שבת.

steps.title: A קל וחומר begins: צרעת overrides the Temple service
steps.stepSummary: The reason is a קל וחומר. Its first step is that צרעת overrides the Temple עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a קל וחומר: just as צרעת, which overrides the Temple service...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's first reading came from a קל וחומר. It starts building that argument, and the argument continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first link is that צרעת 'pushes aside' the עבודה. A כהן with צרעת may not serve in the בית המקדש, and he may not cut off the צרעת mark just so that he can serve. The full argument will show that מילה is even stronger, so it should override שבת too.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a weaker case to a stronger case: if the weaker case has this rule, the stronger case surely has it too.
The skin affliction described in the תורה, which makes a person טמא.
Pushes aside, overrides.
The Temple service done by the כהנים.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here thinking the proof is finished. This is only the first link. On the next amud the גמרא will say that מילה overrides צרעת, and that the עבודה overrides שבת. Only then does the conclusion come: מילה overrides שבת.

phrases.english: It is an a fortiori inference:
Just as leprosy,
phrases.notes: 'וּמָה' starts the first, weaker side of the קל וחומר.

phrases.english: which overrides the Temple service,
phrases.notes: A כהן with צרעת cannot serve, and the mark may not be cut off so that he can serve.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא: וּמָה צָרַעַת שֶׁדּוֹחֶה אֶת הָעֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 33 by starting a קל וחומר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reasoning is a קל וחומר. It begins from the fact that צרעת overrides the Temple עבודה, and it continues in the next lines.
